hazards: PREDICTION DRIFT: the server (ShipBridge.stepMovement l.1230-1280), the pilot (ShipClient.predict l.944-985) and replicas (replica.ts replicaStep l.105-120, server net/Replication.ts l.113) must run identical hooks in identical order. Design answer: all flight/derive/power hooks live ONLY in common and are called from the single stepFlight/rebuild/powerTick call sites, ordered by compile-time (phase, order, id) tuples; server/client halves never contain predicted logic. The remaining drift risk is the hand-copied input plumbing (4 input lists in GameServer, FlightControls object literals at ShipBridge l.1262-1278 and ShipClient l.965-970): the plan.inputs table must generate/replace ALL of them in the same cut that converts a feature, otherwise a half-migrated input silently desyncs. Quantisation (SHIP_PRECISION) must still be applied once at the end; hooks must not carry unrounded state across ticks. Hook inputs like body.cargo (cargoMass + tow load, ShipBridge l.1236) must be summed identically on both sides (client uses player.cargoMass from the pilot row).

CIRCULAR IMPORTS: rebuild.ts already imports strafer.ts (STRAFE_SIDEWAYS) and flight.ts, while strafer.ts imports energy.ts and rebuild.ts types, flight.ts imports anchor.ts/strafer.ts. A registry imported by rebuild.ts, flight.ts and energy.ts that also imports the feature modules (which import those files) creates cycles. Rules: features/types.ts is type-only; features' index.ts may import rebuild/flight/energy but rebuild/flight/energy import ONLY plan.ts via a late-bound getter `getPlan()` that lazily requires the generated FEATURES array (call getPlan() inside functions, never at module scope); the generated features/index.ts is imported only by plan.ts and the package barrel. Add a madge/ts import-cycle check to CUT 1's tests (tooling not present today, the audit did not map cycles). Server/client halves import common only, never each other; common never imports them (server/client registries are keyed by feature id and resolved in their own packages).

COMMON/DIST AND BARREL: the server consumes @space-game/common via common/dist (build:common); stale dist makes server tests pass/fail against old features. Always run `npm run build:common` before server tests, and make the generated barrel (features/index.ts) committed, not build-time only. Do not rely on side-effect registration or vite tree-shaking (explicit array export). Glob order differs by OS (Windows here): the generator must sort by id.

CONCURRENT-EDIT COLLISIONS: GameServer.ts (5,762 lines), ShipBridge.ts (2,453), Game.ts, ShipClient.ts (1,154), ShipRenderer.ts, protocol.ts, partTip.ts, models.mjs are edited by every agent; the working tree currently has uncommitted Strafer/Tow/Repair Beam/Point Defence changes (58 files, ShipBridge 183 lines, ShipClient 142, GameServer 118). Convert Tow only after those are committed. Memory rule: never checkout/restore/stash/reset; agents in separate worktrees must base on a committed tree and the integrator merges; CUT 2's single-line insertions into the god-files should be applied in one short window and announced. rebuild.ts feature block (l.463-535) and flight.ts l.364-526 are shared by CUT 5, 6, 7: strictly sequential there.

PERF IN THE PER-TICK PATH: stepFlight runs per ship per tick on server (every ship, including AI) and in client prediction/replicas; powerTick is the hottest loop. Never look hooks up by string, Map or `find` per tick. Resolve once at startup into frozen per-phase arrays (plan.flight.preJump etc.), and per ship precompute `derived.fxList` (Int8Array of active feature indices) in rebuild so a ship without anchor/strafer/tow loops zero entries. Avoid allocating a FlightCtx per tick: reuse one scratch object per call site (module-level, reset by field, safe because single-threaded but NOT re-entrant: pilotJumpStep calls stepShipPhysics inside a closure, verify no nested stepFlight). Keep closures out of the hook arrays (plain functions taking ctx). Add the microbench gate in verification.

WIRE LAYOUT IS POSITIONAL: pilot row data[13..15], charge groups at CHARGE_GROUPS_AT=16 (up to 24) with extras AFTER the groups (dodge, dodgeSpent, tow), status[8], keyframe tail and CTL bits, binary flags2 (full). The generated tables must reproduce today's indices exactly (features.wire.json append-only, pinned in CUT 1) or an unannounced layout change breaks old clients and the PROTOCOL_WIRE_HASH pin. Extras after the charge groups shift with the group count: generated readers must compute offsets from the group count, never fixed indices. A NEW feature input cannot be added until a longer binary input form exists (flags2 is out of bits): make the generator fail loudly with that message rather than silently overflowing.
